# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Context

Only one task is below 1.0: **case-019-content-vs-code-split (reward 0.75, flaky)** — decomposition_quality 4/5, "Epic Boundaries — solid with one minor overlap". The prior iteration (cand_0001) fixed exactly this cluster but broke 013/014/016 (gate: REJECTED, Δ −0.156, batch reverted). Its 584-line script + 3 enforcement points (decompose 8c, review 2.0 folding, revise re-run gate + must-fix enumeration) had an unbounded blast radius in practice. This iteration re-attacks the SAME cluster with a structurally different, verified-bounded design: enforcement moved to the DECOMPOSER only, two narrow checks instead of four families, fail-open semantics, and every firing condition tested against every file version (not just final artifacts) of all 8 tasks.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Spec-epic authors real content a sibling content epic also authors (E001 "reference example of a correctly packaged tutorial" vs E003 "Author six curated tutorials") | case-019 (reward 0.75; the scored deduction) | Decomposer has no spec-vs-content boundary rule (Step 5 splits code/content/docs but says nothing about a format epic authoring real instances). First review missed it (caught only priority inheritance); the unconditional first revision fixed only that; the terminal re-review then listed the overlap as a minor — too late to be fixed. Scorer: "one minor overlap" → 4/5. | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule) + BEHAVIORAL (detection stochastic, terminal) | missing rule + worked example in decompose Step 5; bundled-script check at 8c; named pattern in review Criterion 3; correction recipe + fix-when-minor in revise |
| 2 | Rollout gate named in scope with no verifying AC (E002 "feature flag / dashboard config gating", no gate AC) | case-019 (same trial; internal re-review minor; may cost AC-Quality points in the scorer's truncated rationale) | Step 7 has no rollout-gate coverage rule; review Criterion 6 doesn't name the pattern. | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule) | missing rule in decompose Step 7; script check; named pattern in review Criterion 6; AC recipe in revise |
| 3 | (prior-iteration process defect, not a task) Enforcement chain blast radius | n/a — the reason 013/014/016 broke under cand_0001 | Mechanical findings folded into the FIRST review drive the unconditional revision; any false positive churns a passing decomposition. cand_0001 verified its script only against FINAL artifacts; intermediate (post-decompose) states differ on revised tasks. | BEHAVIORAL (process) | this iteration: predicates tested against ALL Write/Edit file versions from all 8 transcripts; enforcement wired at decomposer 8c only, fail-open |

Leverage: cluster 1 is the scored deduction (0.75 → 1.0 on 1/8 of val ≈ +0.031 reward); cluster 2 removes the remaining named defect in the same trial. No other cluster exists — 7/8 tasks are solid at 1.0.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | missing rule + worked example | epic-decompose/prompts/decompose-agent.md (Step 5, new "Spec-vs-content boundary" axis bullet) | General rule: a format/schema/standard epic never authors real instances of a sibling content epic's deliverable; validates with a minimal stub, or the content epic's first instance is the reference. Applies to any spec+content strategy. | Yes — BOUNDED: trigger (format epic + sibling non-docs content-authoring epic) verified absent from all 7 passing tasks (019 is the only val task with the structure) |
| 2 | missing rule | epic-decompose/prompts/decompose-agent.md (Step 7, "Rollout-gate coverage" bullet) | Any rollout gate named in scope needs a verifying AC; human-approval gates and CI gating checks explicitly excluded. | Yes — BOUNDED: gate-in-scope-without-AC verified unique to 019-E002 across all 8 tasks (all file versions) |
| 1+2 | NEW bundled script (code enforcement) | epic-decompose/scripts/check_decomposition.py (341 lines, real code, `--self-check` 5/5 PASS, py_compile clean, stdlib only) | Two mechanical checks — spec-content overlap, gating-AC gap — each finding names file + epic + defect + exact fix. Dependency-free frontmatter/section parser; excludes docs-authoring epics and the named non-defect classes. | Yes — BOUNDED: exit 0 / zero findings on all 7 passing tasks' final artifacts AND every intermediate version; exactly the 2 target findings on 019 |

Two-path invocation covers both runtime layouts. | Yes — on passing tasks the script exits 0 (verified); only behavior delta is one extra Bash call printing OK |
| 1 | named pattern in rubric (+ do-not-flag guidance) | epic-decompose/prompts/review-agent.md (Criterion 3 Check) | Names the spec-vs-content overlap pattern with severity split and the correct fix; negative guidance lists the actual near-miss classes (docs epics, stubs/fixtures, console-report "examples") so a primed reviewer doesn't false-flag. | Yes — no passing task's first or final review lists an overlap-class issue (verified from all 8 transcripts); no passing task has the trigger structure |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- `check_decomposition.py --self-check`: 5 synthetic fixtures (clean, spec-content overlap, gating-ac gap, docs-authoring excluded, gate-AC-present) — ALL PASS.
- On all 8 tasks' exact final artifacts (extracted from trajectories): **exit 0, zero findings on all 7 passing tasks** (013: 7 epics, 014: 6, 015: 4, 016: 4, 017: 2, 018: 5, 020: 7 incl. branch file in glob scope); on case-019 exactly `FINDING [spec-content] RHAISTRAT-9019-E001` + `FINDING [gating-ac] RHAISTRAT-9019-E002` — the two defects the internal re-review listed and the scorer's "one minor overlap" names.
- On **every intermediate file version** (per-file version histories reconstructed from ALL Write/Edit tool calls in all 8 transcripts — the states the 8c check would actually see): predicates fire on ZERO passing-task versions; only 019-E001/E002 (whose versions are unchanged post-decompose — 019's reviser only touched E001's priority field and the summary).
- 8c invocation snippet executed verbatim in BOTH runtime layouts (`skills/epic-decompose/epic-decompose/scripts/…` and single-nested `skills/epic-decompose/scripts/…`): correct findings on 019 artifacts in both; fallback path resolves.
- Fix loop closed: applied the findings' stated fixes to 019's E001 (stub restatement of both "reference example" claims) and E002 (gate AC) → re-run exits 0. The check also caught a partial fix (second "reference example" occurrence in E001's ACs) — it cannot be satisfied by a half-fix.
- Step 5 rule trigger vs traces: 019 is the only val task with a non-docs content-authoring epic beside a format-defining epic; the worked example uses a different domain (notebook packaging format vs curated notebook library).
- Gating rule trigger vs traces: gate-vocab-in-scope-without-gate-AC unique to 019-E002; 014-E005 ("enabled by default") has a gate AC → not flagged; 013-E004 (CI gating check) doesn't match rollout-gate vocabulary.
- Reviewer rubric additions vs traces: extracted every `decomp-review.md` issues write from all 8 transcripts (first reviews AND re-reviews) — no passing task ever lists an overlap-class or gating-AC issue; the do-not-flag lists name the actual near-miss classes observed in passing tasks.
- Revise must-fix sentence vs traces: passing tasks' listed minors match neither named class → their leave/fix latitude is unchanged.
- SKILL.md description: states when to use, 305 chars < 1024 limit → clears the validation warning recorded in rejected.jsonl.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none — serial. Only ONE non-passing task; coverage came from programmatic scans (all-8-tasks artifact extraction + version-history reconstruction), which cost ~6 turns and made every SAFE claim a measurement.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: cand_0001's PROCESS.md and JOURNAL/RESULT (its diff.patch is truncated at 144 lines — only DIAGNOSIS.json, not the capability edits; noted in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md). Used its RESULT (fixed={019}, broke={013,014,016}) to keep the cluster and redesign the enforcement: dropped reviewer-side script folding, revise-side re-run gate, must-fix enumeration, and all structural/broad checks; kept decomposer-side rules, one narrow script, fail-open 8c wiring, and bounded recipes.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The 8c boundary check is **advisory/fail-open by design** — never make it a hard completion gate (a hard gate that can't run or that false-fires stalls/churns decompositions; that is the shape of cand_0001's regression).
- The check's firing conditions were verified against **every file version**, not just final artifacts — keep that bar for any new check.
- The reviewer prompt contains NO script-running step and the reviser has NO re-run gate — enforcement lives at the producer (decomposer). Do not re-add consumer-side folding without re-proving boundedness.
- The revise must-fix list is exactly two named defect classes; all other minors keep latitude (015/016/017/018/020 pass with observation minors).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- **docs-priority derivation (019-E004 P2 vs Major→P1)**: the scorer's visible feedback EXPLICITLY accepts P2 ("acceptable under the docs-exemption rule") — zero scored upside, nonzero churn risk. The internal re-review's minor stays unfixed, as in the seed.
- **gate_failure_impact / gated_by completeness check**: fires on passing 020's post-decompose state (its first review flagged exactly this as majors; the reviser fixed them). Decompose-time fixing would change 020's trajectory without verified fix-path equivalence. Same skip cand_0001 made — still correct.
- **Structural checks in the script** (branch metadata, epic_count, draft-ID refs, missing ai-signals files): conventions are ambiguous (epic_count may count main-plan only or all epics incl. branches — 016 has branch files), and cand_0001's rejection is consistent with broad structural checks false-firing; the review rubric already covers them by hand.
- **Loop-semantics changes** (revise again after a passing re-review): unbounded — passing tasks end with unfixed observation minors by design.
- **Scorer feedback truncation** (~1288 chars): framework issue, already recorded in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.

Written to ./DIAGNOSIS.json (see file). Summary: 2 clusters on case-019 (A: spec-epic/content-epic boundary overlap — the scored deduction; B: rollout-gate AC gap), fixed via one new bundled script + decomposer rules + reviewer pattern-naming + reviser recipes, all verified bounded against every file version of all 8 tasks; cluster 3 (prior enforcement-chain blast radius) addressed by design.
